text: rwb-reporting builds the steering read model from the events of its producers — CaseCreated (EV-01), CaseAllocated (EV-02), CaseStateChanged (EV-05), DecisionRecorded (EV-08), TreatmentApproved (EV-10), NoticeDispatched (EV-14), NoticeDelivered (EV-15) and AgentRunCompleted (EV-28) — by replaying the bounded window of a business date into a run-scoped fact view of the workflow, deduplicated on the event id, with no fact table and no v_ace_* read, and the publish, freshness and hold live in rwb_reporting.
why: The legacy story reads six in-process interfaces and two ACE views; the context pack gives the service three tables only, Arch v5 removes the data lake and DP-17 moves reporting onto events, and no source fixes a read-model mechanism.
read: RWB-E2-009 sections 3, 4, 11, 12 and 13; Event and Messaging Design v4 events sheet; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-11 and DP-17; P9 context pack (three tables, connection matrix row of P9).
confirm: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-treatment, rwb-comms and rwb-agent
impact: Medium: a change to the read-model mechanism changes one activity and no measure definition; the counts and rates keep their rule.

text: JOB-15 is deployed as the Temporal Schedule reportingMeasuresDaily at 01:30 on the task queue rwb-reporting in namespace rwb-recovery, opening one execution per business date with the six activities checkDataReady, loadReadModel, loadAgentFacts, computeMeasures, reconcileCounts and publishDay; the names are the design baseline of this split, a rerun joins the execution of its business date, the freshness check reuses the read that RWB-P1-E1013-APP declares and the extract hand-over runs on the rwb-integration queue per the connection matrix, and no Quartz row and no Spring Batch descriptor is created.
why: The legacy story schedules JOB-15 as a Quartz and Spring Batch job and names no target workflow or activity; DP-10 replaces a Quartz job with a Temporal Schedule through the workflow kit, and the matrix shows the P1 and P2 calls as Temporal.
read: RWB-E2-009 sections 4, 12 and 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10 and DP-13; P9 context pack (task queue rwb-reporting, namespace rwb-recovery, job JOB-15, connection matrix row of P9).
applied_in: Sections 4, 12.5, 12.6 and 13 of RWB-P9-E2009-APP and sections 12.5 and 12.6 of RWB-P9-E2009-CON
confirm: Solution architect with the platform workflow kit owner and the reporting service owner
impact: Medium: a renamed workflow or Schedule changes one registration and one alert label and no business rule.

text: The INT-19 extract to the data lake is replaced by a hand-over of the published day's rows to rwb-integration as an activity on its queue, carrying the business date as the freshness stamp, so the 07:30 Power BI refresh reads the same snapshot rows as SCR-37; no data-lake object, trailer or lake client exists, and the file shape Power BI reads is fixed by no source.
why: RWB-E2-009 AC1, AC4 and section 4 name an INT-19 extract and a data lake, Arch v5 removes the lake, INT-19 and INT-20 under DP-17, and the FSD P9 still names Power BI and the data lake as integration points.
read: RWB-E2-009 sections 2, 4, 7 and 12; TSD P9 v2 T5.1 (INT-19); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 9; P9 context pack (no data lake, reporting from events).
confirm: Solution architect with the owner of rwb-integration and the Reporting and BI analyst role
impact: Medium: the published rows are the single source either way; if the hand-over is dropped, only the Power BI path changes and the screen is unaffected.

text: AGENT_ACCEPTANCE and AGENT_OVERRIDE are computed per agent and version from the agent runs of the business date read on RWB-P10-E1063-CON and from AgentRunCompleted (EV-28), keeping the legacy rule that accepted is over all recommendations and override is over all recommendations, and a pair with no run writes no rate and shows No runs.
why: The legacy story reads AgentMonitorApi.runFacts of P10 and RWB-E1-063, the plan scopes the agent facts as RWB-P10-E1063-CON, and the connection matrix shows no REST or event row from P10 to P9, so both a contract and an event are named.
read: RWB-E2-009 sections 3, 4, 7 and 12; Event and Messaging Design v4 (EV-28); Work Package B2-P9-002 story line (C row RWB-P10-E1063-CON); TSD P9 v2 T7 (NFR-066).
confirm: Solution architect with the owner of rwb-agent and the reporting service owner
impact: Medium: the rates are counts over the run facts, so a change of the agent contract changes the mapping and not the rule.

text: RWB-P9-E2009-CON is published as an increment on the parent tag of RWB-P9-E1013-CON: measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish keep the field sets of DF-RPT-031 to DF-RPT-058 and the standard columns that the parent declares, this key adds only the unique key on the business date, the index on status and the index on (measure_code, business_date, product_group), and the baselineValue of the Measure shape is derived from the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 rather than stored in a new column; the legacy migration V2_009__measure_publish.sql is not reused.
why: The legacy story treats measure_publish as new for E2-009 and asks for a dimension and a baseline field, while the parent slice of the same service already creates the three tables and the same operation, and no column carries a baseline value.
read: RWB-E2-009 sections 11, 12 and 13; TSD P9 v2 T3.0 and T3.1; RWB-P9-E1013-CON sections 12.1 and 12.7; RWB-P9-E1013-APP sections 1 and 3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15.
applied_in: Sections 3, 11 and 12.7 of RWB-P9-E2009-APP and sections 1, 7, 11 and 12.7 of RWB-P9-E2009-CON
confirm: Data architect with the contract owners of rwb-reporting
impact: Low: one writer of the three tables and one tag chain, so a later change of a field set is a parent version and not a second baseline.

text: The contract baseline is one tagged version v1 whose element names for the case-list, agent-run and reference-data declarations and for the two owner-queue activities are a review baseline that their owners may correct as a patch, with a fake per declaration and per subscription, no business value frozen, and no element of the data lake, INT-19, INT-20 or of the service's own event published; a shape change opens v2 and the tag stays buildable.
why: No published document fixes the target element names of the consumed declarations or the envelope naming of the eight subscriptions, and the tag is what lets the application and deployment stories start on Day 1.
read: RWB-E2-009 sections 12 and 13; TSD P9 v2 Appendix T-A and T5.3; Event and Messaging Design v4; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11, R7.2 s12 and R8.2.
confirm: Contract owner of rwb-reporting with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-agent, rwb-source-data, rwb-integration and rwb-decision
impact: Medium: a corrected element name is a patch to the same tag and no consumer rebuilds; a shape change is a new version.

text: Every deployment value of the release — the login secret reference, the connection pool, the replica counts, the resource requests, the topic retention and the consumer offset policy, the Schedule time zone and catch-up window, the backfill limit, the six alert thresholds and the four series windows — is a value of the environment and is tuned per environment, and the run message ID of the flag-off and run-not-started paths is allocated with the message catalogue owner.
why: No source in this key names a deployment value, TSD P9 v2 Appendix T-B leaves the non-functional targets open under DL11, and the run message ID does not exist in the legacy message set.
read: RWB-E2-009 sections 4, 13 and 14; TSD P9 v2 Appendix T-B; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R9; P9 context pack (names only).
confirm: DevOps team with the platform administrator, the observability owner and the event platform owner
impact: Low: the values are environment settings; the alerts and the runbook entries are the release gate.

text: The release is prepared without an approval and the first environment is non-production; the hashes of the release carry Draft (realignment v1), the Schedule and the worker versioning policy name the build ID of the release, and a rollback re-registers the Schedule against the previous build while a running execution finishes on the build that started it.
why: No approval is required in this run, the plan fixes no build ID or versioning policy, and the story must still state how a rollback behaves on a Scheduled workflow.
read: Work Package B2-P9-002 story line (Status Draft, release 31 December 2026); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10, R7.1 and R9; TSD P9 v2 Appendix T-B (DL35 deployment slots).
confirm: DevOps team with the workflow kit owner and the reporting service owner
impact: Low: the rollback rule is a deployment policy and changes no business behaviour.
